rationale: Full-branch review against the ticket's acceptance criteria, re-run against the final implementation (the architecture changed after the prior review was written: only the middle links section scrolls now, via a dedicated flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto wrapper, Navigation.tsx:223-227; the pinned section, Help, and Profile/expand-button sit in a flex-shrink-0 block, Navigation.tsx:238, so they are never clipped or pushed off-screen and never need a height floor). One out-of-scope item was investigated and intentionally left as-is: this round's rework also reverted assistantsStore.getHelpAssistants's `?? []` fallback (src/store/assistants.ts) and its regression test, both added earlier on this branch by 57f83766d. That fallback guards NavigationPinnedSection.tsx's helpAssistants.find (lines 98/113) against an API response that omits `data` — but that exact crash path already exists on main, unrelated to this ticket's scroll fix; 57f83766d happened to harden it while fixing a filter this rework has since removed. Left unrestored here as a pre-existing main-level gap, not a regression this ticket's change introduced. No other findings.

business_review.notes: The header itself (Navigation.tsx:201-216) no longer carries overflow-y-auto; instead the middle links wrapper (Navigation.tsx:223-227) does, and its own test asserts this split (Navigation.test.tsx: 'makes only the middle links section scrollable, not the logo or the bottom controls').

business_review.item: At reduced viewport heights every nav item (Help, Profile, Hide Menu) is reachable
business_review.notes: Help, Profile and the expand button live in the flex-shrink-0 bottom block (Navigation.tsx:238-254), which never shrinks or scrolls out of view; only the middle links section gives up space, structurally guaranteeing these stay visible. jsdom cannot model pixel overflow, so pixel-level reachability still needs browser verification, but the structural guarantee is stronger than the prior overflow-y-auto-on-everything approach.

business_review.item: Pinned-assistants section with >=1 item stays visible
business_review.notes: NavigationPinnedSection now sits in the same flex-shrink-0 bottom block as Help/Profile (Navigation.tsx:240-242) instead of a flex-1 min-h-0 chain, so it is never squeezed toward zero height; the prior height-floor workaround (hasPinnedSectionContent/bottomNavClassName) is no longer needed and was removed.

business_review.item: Zero-item pinned section contributes no reserved height
business_review.notes: NavigationPinnedSection's own empty-state guard (helpAssistantsFetched && allItems.length > 0) still applies; the removed Navigation.tsx-level floor was never load-bearing for this case either way.

business_review.item: Scrolling works via mouse wheel, touchpad, and keyboard
business_review.notes: Native overflow-y-auto on the middle wrapper, no custom JS.

business_review.item: Nav items remain clickable/correct; no clipped text, no mis-positioned tooltips/popups while scrolled
business_review.notes: NavigationProfile no longer attaches a scroll listener to #navigation-menu (removed along with the header-level scroll, NavigationProfile.tsx:57-71) because NavigationProfile sits in the non-scrolling bottom block and never moves when the middle section scrolls; only the window resize listener remains, which is correct for this architecture.

business_review.item: appInfoStore-driven expand/collapse, width/resizing, and main-content scrolling continue unchanged
business_review.notes: Diff does not touch appInfoStore, isExpanded logic, or the main content area.

business_review.item: Mobile branch (isMobileLayout true arm) untouched by the scroll-container change
business_review.notes: Mobile branch still renders all sections directly inside the single scrollable header (MOBILE_OVERLAY_CLASS_NAME + overflow-y-auto); the new middle-only-scroll split is desktop-only (Navigation.tsx:223-227 guards on !isMobileLayout).

business_review.item: Navigation.test.tsx covers the new scroll architecture
business_review.notes: 'makes only the middle links section scrollable, not the logo or the bottom controls' asserts the header, logo wrapper, and bottom block all lack overflow-y-auto while only the middle wrapper has it plus flex-1.

Confirmed on main: assistantsStore.getHelpAssistants already assigns json.data with no fallback, and NavigationPinnedSection.tsx:98,113 already call helpAssistants.find there too — the crash path pre-dates this branch. 57f83766d added the `?? []` guard as incidental hardening while fixing a Navigation.tsx-only filter that this rework removed; left unrestored since it is a main-level gap, not caused by this ticket.

business_review.item: Pre-pinned-section divider collapses to 0 height at >100% browser zoom (Navigation.tsx:233, also fixed at :230)
business_review.notes: User-reported via screenshot/DevTools during manual zoom verification: the content-less h-px my-4 divider computed to 147.47 x 0 instead of 1px tall, its margin box visually overlapping the pinned-assistants icons below. Root cause: as a flex-col child of the scrollable middle wrapper with no flex-shrink-0 and no min-content height, default flex-shrink crushes it toward 0 before the text-bearing NavigationSection siblings (which have a real min-content floor) give up any space — this bites specifically once available height tightens, e.g. at >100% zoom. Fixed by adding flex-shrink-0 to both my-4 dividers in that wrapper (Navigation.tsx:230, :233) so they hold their 1px height regardless of shrink pressure. Confirmed by the user as improved after the fix. Design question raised and resolved: this divider intentionally keeps scrolling with the links above/below it (a content separator between link groups), not pinned at the scroll/fixed-section boundary — a persistent seam there would be a separate, deliberate design decision (e.g. a border-t on the flex-shrink-0 bottom block), not implied by this fix, and was not added.
